findings.highlight: It was probably a typical dinner...except it didn't feel that way.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺以外は概ねいつも通りの夕食だったと思う。
findings.governingReading: Dinner was normal for everyone except Shirou; distracted by the changing-room incident, he could not even tell how the food tasted.
findings.explanation: Shirou's private loss of taste becomes a general atypical dinner and loss of appetite.

findings.highlight: A wave of vertigo washes over me.
findings.evidenceJa: かつん、と目眩らしきものが通り過ぎた。
findings.governingReading: Something like vertigo passes through Shirou, and he can only just understand that it is the light of magical energy.
findings.explanation: A barely recognized flash of magical light becomes a clearly identified energy ripple.

findings.highlight: "Yes, I was waiting for you. You fortified your body with Saber during the day, right? Then we need to train your mind at night."
findings.evidenceJa: 「ええ、待ってたわ。昼間はセイバーと体の方を鍛えてたんでしょ？　なら夜は中身を鍛えないとね」
findings.governingReading: After Saber trained his body by day, Rin proposes training what is inside him at night—his magical constitution and circuits.
findings.explanation: Training Shirou's magical interior becomes training his mind.

findings.highlight: Tohsaka seems happy, ready to teach.
findings.evidenceJa: 教える気まんまんなのか、遠坂はなにやら嬉しそうだ。
findings.governingReading: Shirou notices Rin's enthusiasm for teaching, contrasts her with Saber, then explicitly sets aside whether Rin is suited to the job.
findings.explanation: “Anyway” removes Shirou's reservation about Rin's teaching aptitude. Her enthusiasm consequently reads more like evidence that she will be a good teacher.

findings.highlight: "Huh? Well, I just said I don't have a Magic Crest. My old man had one, but I didn't inherit it."
findings.evidenceJa: 「えっ……いや、魔術刻印はないって言ったんだが。親父は持ってたみたいだけど、譲られはしなかった」
findings.governingReading: Shirou says his father seems to have had a Magic Crest, but it was not passed to him.
findings.explanation: Kiritsugu apparently possessing a crest becomes certain possession.

findings.highlight: "Of course not. If I knew, I would have never let you go out and do stuff on your own. Sure, I knew you weren't fully trained, but if you don't have a Magic Crest, you aren't even a mage."
findings.evidenceJa: 「そんな訳ないでしょ。知ってたら一人でなんか行動させなかったわよ。……そりゃあ半人前だなって思ってたけど、魔術刻印がないならそもそも魔術師じゃないじゃない、士郎は」
findings.governingReading: Had Rin known he lacked a crest, she would never have allowed him to operate or take action alone.
findings.explanation: Rin's refusal to let Shirou act alone becomes a vague ban on going out and doing stuff.

findings.highlight: "Well, whatever. This just means I have to teach you everything from scratch. But since you know what Magic Crests are, you know what a mage is.
findings.evidenceJa: 「—まあいいわ。そういう事なら一から説明してあげる。魔術刻印がなんなのかを知るって事は、魔術師ってものを知るって事だから。
findings.governingReading: Understanding Magic Crests means understanding what a mage is; this explains why Rin will teach the subject from the beginning.
findings.explanation: Rin's reason for explaining Magic Crests becomes an assertion that Shirou already understands them. The Japanese says learning about crests will explain what being a mage means.

findings.highlight: Some may use magecraft via their own means, while some may do it by paying a price of some sort.
findings.evidenceJa: 自分だけの精神力をもって魔術を使用する者もいれば、　自分以外の代価をもって魔術を使用する者もいる。
findings.governingReading: Some practitioners use their own unique spiritual or mental power, while others pay a price external to themselves.
findings.explanation: Personal mental force becomes unspecified personal means.

findings.highlight: "Listen. Mages who don't have so much history, like you, employ something that already has taken form to use magical energy.
findings.evidenceJa: 「いい士郎？　積み重ねた歴史が浅い魔術師……ようするに士郎の事ね……は、“すでに形式あるもの”を以って魔力と成すの。
findings.governingReading: Mages with little accumulated history use things that already possess established form as magical power.
findings.explanation: Saber explains that mages with little inherited history use things with an established form as magical power. The English makes those things merely a means “to use magical energy,” losing their role as the power resource.

findings.highlight: "It's similar to my jewels you saw earlier. Once a certain magecraft is mastered, a mage can physically 'hold' that magecraft.
findings.evidenceJa: 「さっきの宝石と似てるかな。一つの魔術を極めるとね、魔術師にはその魔術が“手に取れる”ようになるの。
findings.governingReading: Once magecraft is mastered, it can be felt as though it were taken in hand, despite being a shapeless formula.
findings.explanation: A quoted tactile metaphor becomes literal physical holding.

findings.highlight: Do you know that feeling of getting ahold of magecraft, even though it's typically shapeless and simply devised?"
findings.evidenceJa: 本来ならカタチのない、ただの公式にすぎない魔術を“手に取れる”感覚ってわかる？」
findings.governingReading: Magecraft is normally a shapeless formula or system.
findings.explanation: A shapeless formula becomes something simply devised.

findings.highlight: Magecraft that goes beyond the realm of principle and becomes a part of you then becomes tangible.
findings.evidenceJa: 扱われる式という域を超えて、もはや自分自身となった魔術っていうのはカタチに残せるのよ。
findings.governingReading: Magecraft that transcends being an operated formula, becomes the mage's own self and can be left in tangible form is a feat that establishes unstable magecraft.
findings.explanation: A spell exceeding the level of a formula and becoming the self is rendered through principle and authentication.

findings.highlight: "And when a mage is on the brink of death, they pass down their great accomplishments to their successor in the form of a crest. It's their way of telling their successor to go further, to places they were unable to reach, and that their crest may be of some use to them.
findings.evidenceJa: 「で、魔術師は死ぬ間際に、自分が成し得た偉業を刻印として後継者に譲るのよ。これをやるから、自分が成し得なかった地点に到達しろ。もしかしたらワシが残した刻印が何かの役に立つかもしれん、ってね。
findings.governingReading: While voicing an ancestor's bequest, Rin switches to the old-person first-person ワシ: perhaps the crest I left will help you.
findings.explanation: Rin's old-mage impersonation disappears.

findings.highlight: "It IS useful! An ordinary mage would consider a single crest to be like a security blanket. It's THAT helpful!
findings.evidenceJa: 「立つわよ！　普通に魔術師やってれば、刻印一つで左うちわっていうぐらい役に立つわ！
findings.governingReading: For an ordinary mage, one crest is useful enough to let them live comfortably and prosper, though it still cannot reach the lineage's ultimate destination.
findings.explanation: A crest enabling a life of ease becomes a security blanket.

findings.highlight: The Magic Crest gets more complex as it passes from generation to generation, but it's also a constraint mages can't escape."
findings.evidenceJa: そうして複雑さを増し、深い歴史を刻んだものが魔術刻印—魔術師にとって、逃れようのない縛りってこと」
findings.governingReading: Generational additions increase complexity and inscribe a deep history; that accumulated object is the Magic Crest and an inescapable bond.
findings.explanation: The deep history engraved in the crest disappears.

findings.highlight: "Huh. Then doesn't that mean you can engrave the crests onto anyone. If magic circles are all you need, then you can draw as many as you want as long as you know the shape."
findings.evidenceJa: 「…………ふむ。それじゃあさ、別に刻印は誰に刻んでもいいって事にならないか？　魔法陣なら、カタチさえ知っていれば幾つでも描けるじゃないか」
findings.governingReading: Shirou asks whether that means a crest could be engraved on anyone.
findings.explanation: Shirou's first question is punctuated as a statement.

findings.highlight: In my case it's on my left arm. It covers my entire arm from my shoulders to my hand. It doesn't show up as long as I'm not using it, so I don't have to hide it like with Command Spells."
findings.evidenceJa: わたしの場合は左腕。肩から手までびっしりね。ただ魔術刻印は使わなければ浮かび上がらないから、令呪と違って隠す必要はないわ」
findings.governingReading: Rin's crest covers her left arm from shoulder to hand and appears only in use.
findings.explanation: Rin's single left shoulder becomes multiple shoulders.

findings.highlight: If a family has multiple siblings, typically any not chosen to be the successor would not be taught magecraft and would instead live an ordinary life. The Magic Crest can't be passed down to them, so there's no point in them being a mage."
findings.evidenceJa: その家に兄弟がいた場合、どちらかは魔術を教えられずに一般人として暮らすのが常なのよ。だって、魔術刻印を渡せないんだから、魔術師として大成されてもあまり意味がないもの」
findings.governingReading: Because the crest cannot be transferred to the other sibling, there is little point in training that sibling to great accomplishment as a mage.
findings.explanation: Little value in an unchosen sibling becoming a great mage becomes no point in being a mage at all.

findings.highlight: But if someone asked me how I feel about Saber in other senses, I wouldn't know how to answer.
findings.evidenceJa: ただそれ以外の部分でセイバーをどう思っているかと言われると、返答に困ってしまう。
findings.governingReading: Shirou can affirm Saber as an ally but cannot name his other feelings because, in the recalled instant, his proper or ordinary emotions were taken from him.
findings.explanation: Loss of normal emotion becomes loss of all sense.

findings.highlight: "I do. There's nothing about her I don't like really.
findings.evidenceJa: 「好きよ。だって嫌いになる要素がないじゃない。
findings.governingReading: Rin plainly says she likes Saber and lists strength, courtesy and beauty; Shirou repeats that Rin likes her, making Rin flustered.
findings.explanation: Rin's direct liking of Saber becomes a balance of liked and disliked traits.

findings.highlight: "I figured as much. You're never sarcastic or cynical. I bet you think of me as loud and annoying."
findings.evidenceJa: 「……そうでしょうよ。嫌味とか皮肉とか口にしなさそうだものね、士郎は。ええ、どうせわたしのコトなんて口うるさい嫌味なヤツだとか思ってるでしょ」
findings.governingReading: Rin assumes Shirou sees her as a mouthy or nagging, caustic person because she speaks in sarcasm and irony.
findings.explanation: Rin's self-description as nagging and sarcastic becomes loud and annoying.
